decisions.decision: T-3-08 threat-model mitigation amended 2026-07-26 (attempt #2, actual root cause, CONFIRMED WORKING live): added CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_SITEPACKAGES=1 env var + check_hashes=if_fast_else_skip boto config fallback + a gsutil version -l pre-flight verification cell
decisions.rationale: Confirmed via GoogleCloudPlatform/gsutil GitHub issue #1429: gsutil (part of Google Cloud SDK) runs its own bundled, isolated Python interpreter, completely separate from the Colab kernel's Python. The earlier crcmod reinstall (260726-gj6) succeeded in the KERNEL's Python but was invisible to gsutil's bundled interpreter, so the CRC32C hash computation stayed on the slow pure-Python path regardless of destination — explaining why moving off Drive didn't help. CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_SITEPACKAGES=1 makes gsutil's bundled interpreter fall back to the kernel's site-packages where crcmod's C extension actually landed. As a safety net (the GitHub issue notes this fallback can fail on Python ABI mismatches), check_hashes=if_fast_else_skip (gsutil's own officially-sanctioned partial integrity-check skip, only triggers when the C extension is genuinely unavailable) was also configured via a /content/.boto file. A pre-flight cell running gsutil version -l lets the user confirm success BEFORE attempting the full 11.6GB download again. User's live re-run confirmed serve_policy.py now starts successfully (~130s) — this diagnosis was correct.

decisions.decision: vla/__init__.py's optional-import guards broadened from except ImportError to except Exception for both OFTBackend and Pi0Backend (2026-07-26, quick task 260726-hw8, CONFIRMED WORKING live)
decisions.rationale: With the server now starting successfully, the very next cell (the literal VLA-04 proof, `from libero.libero.vla import Pi0Backend, run_suite`) crashed with `ValueError: numpy.dtype size changed, may indicate binary incompatibility` raised deep inside transformers/torch's import chain while importing OFTBackend — not an ImportError, so the existing `except ImportError:` guard (whose own comment already claimed to 'degrade gracefully' across kernels with incompatible dependency stacks, per D-06) did not catch it, crashing the whole package import including the unrelated Pi0Backend the cell actually needed. Broadened both guards (not just OFTBackend's) since they share the identical documented intent and the same class of failure could symmetrically hit Pi0Backend's guard in Notebook A's kernel. Verified via the existing local pytest suite (7 passed) AND the user's live re-run, which got past this crash entirely.

context_notes: Phase 3 (VLA Inference Loop) is functionally very close to done — the hard engineering (shared VLABackend interface, OFTBackend, eval_loop, Pi0Backend, both notebooks) is complete and verified for the OFT path, and seven real bugs have now been found+fixed via live Colab debugging — two in OFT's path during 03-02, five in π0's path during 03-03 Task 4, all on 2026-07-26: 260726-epz (config-name drift, confirmed), 260726-gj6 (checkpoint-download destination, later found insufficient), 260726-hbb (the actual download-reliability root cause, confirmed), 260726-hw8 (vla/__init__.py import-guard crash on numpy ABI error, confirmed), 260726-io0 (missing robosuite/mujoco/bddl/gym simulation stack — a genuine planning gap, not yet confirmed live, requires a full restart-from-top run). Four of five π0-path fixes are now confirmed working live; only the newest (io0) awaits its first live test. Discovered mid-session: this repo's LIBERO/ is its own nested git repo, entirely gitignored by the main repo, but on case-insensitive macOS a pre-existing (Phase 1) convention has files landing under a lowercase 'libero/' path tracked by the MAIN repo's git (not LIBERO's own git) — this is accepted/pre-existing, not something to 'fix' mid-phase. Also discovered: Colab kernels cache Python module imports across cell re-runs — re-syncing a fixed source file via the unzip cell does NOT reload already-imported modules; a genuine Runtime > Restart session is required, not just re-running cells. This caused one confusing false-repeat-error round-trip during debugging; flagged as advisory for any future Colab debugging in this project. Lesson from 260726-epz: openpi tracks main with no pinned release — its LIBERO config names (pi0_fast_libero/pi0_libero) were deprecated in favor of pi05_libero between plan-time and first live run; re-verify openpi's serve_policy.py/README/config.py directly against source before trusting any previously-researched config name if this project's openpi checkout advances again. Lesson from 260726-gj6+260726-hbb (important — a misdiagnosis happened here, later corrected and confirmed): an identical gsutil failure ('N files/objects could not be transferred' after crcmod C-extension warnings) persisted across two different download destinations (Drive-mounted, then local disk), which falsified the first root-cause theory (Drive FUSE unreliability). The ACTUAL cause was that gsutil (Google Cloud SDK) uses its own bundled, isolated Python interpreter that never sees packages pip-installed into the Colab kernel — so 'pip install crcmod' in a notebook cell does NOT make gsutil see the compiled extension, regardless of where the download is going. The general lesson: when a fix doesn't change an error's exact wording/behavior at all after a live re-test, suspect the fix targeted a coincidental/secondary factor, not the actual mechanism — re-derive from the raw traceback and the specific tool's own architecture rather than patching the most visible symptom a second time. This paid off: the corrected fix (260726-hbb) was confirmed working on the very next live re-run. Lesson from 260726-hw8: a defensive optional-import guard (`except ImportError:`) that exists specifically to let a shared module import successfully across kernels with different/incompatible dependency stacks needs to catch the actual class of failure those incompatible stacks can produce (ValueError from numpy ABI mismatches, not just ModuleNotFoundError) — confirmed working live. Lesson from 260726-io0: each fix so far has surfaced the NEXT problem down the line rather than closing the loop entirely — this is expected given Notebook B never had a real live run before today, but it means every 'fix confirmed working' should be read as 'this specific error is gone', not 'the notebook now works end-to-end', until a full top-to-bottom run actually completes the VLA-04 smoke test. Also: when a genuinely missing dependency/setup step is found (not a version-drift or environment quirk like the others), check whether the OTHER already-working notebook in this project solved the same category of problem before — Notebook A's Block A/B restart pattern was directly reusable here almost verbatim.
